correctness.rationale: Published Theorem 11/Proposition 18 reduce periodic antisquare avoidance to eight explicit forbidden factors. The 2-to-1 cyclic difference map converts these to an alternating 0-run >=2, 1-run in {2,4} grammar. That is equivalent to strict-minority occurrence gaps in {2} or [4,infinity) with no neighboring 2s. Marked circular gaps and cyclic nonadjacency give the stated exact composition sum; transfer-matrix log determinant gives the full bivariate rational series. Characteristic-root decomposition gives the exact asymptotics, and a simple aperiodic dominant root gives Gaussian convergence, with positive variance bounded in exact rational arithmetic. The source dependency and finite verification limits are explicitly stated; independent exhaustive antisquare checks n<=15 and exact coefficient checks n<=19 agree.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a complete length-and-composition enumeration, including a sharp feasible minority cutoff and its extremizers, for a canonical antisquare-avoidance subshift. Exact labeled-periodic counts and a positive-variance Gaussian law are natural tools for finite-word constrained coding and periodic-orbit analysis; they answer more than the previously known exponential order of unrestricted linear counts. The precise statistic is the intrinsic minority symbol count and is mathematically motivated by the forbidden-language grammar.
